[{"number":825,"title":"Replace per-file cache TTLs with a published manifest","body":"Closes #314

## What changed

`scraper/normalize.py`'s `write_derived_outputs` now writes `site/data/manifest.json` in the same run as everything else it produces: `{v: 1, files: {relpath: sha256}}` for venues.json, every day file, and the three `normalized/*.min.json` sidecars. `write_json` returns the hash of exactly the bytes it wrote, so `build_manifest` costs nothing extra to compute — no second read or re-hash pass.

`site/shared/data-cache.js` fetches that manifest **uncached** on every load (never itself cached — a stale copy would carry a valid hash of itself) and compares it, file by file, to the hash each Cache Storage entry was last fetched under. That replaces the four guessed TTLs (4 days for the catalogue, 1 day for availability, 1 hour for the day file, a week for descriptions) with a check that is both longer-lived (a file is reused indefinitely once nothing about it has changed) and never stale (a file is re-fetched the moment its published hash moves — no earlier, no later). `js/app.js` and `plan/plan.js` are updated to fetch the manifest and pass it into every `cachedFetchJson` call.

When the manifest itself can't be fetched, freshness is treated as **unknown**, never as "nothing changed": every `cachedFetchJson` call for that load skips the cache and goes straight to the network. The data still loads correctly either way — this only forgoes the reuse, never the correctness of what's rendered, so there's no "everything shows as unknown" failure mode to guard against.

`site/data/` was regenerated through `scraper/normalize.py --minify-from-master` (never hand-edited) — the only new byte anywhere in it is `manifest.json` itself; every other file it wrote came back byte-for-byte identical.

## Scope: the three overlapping mechanisms

Per the issue's ask, here's what happened to each:

- **Manifest** (new, this PR) — decides *"is my cached copy the published one?"*, replacing the TTLs.
- **Join fingerprint + 90% coverage floor** (`site/plan/plan.js`'s `joinIsSound`) — **kept**, not retired. It answers a different question the manifest can't: a deploy landing *between* the manifest fetch and the catalogue/availability fetches it drives can still hand back a pair from two different publishes. The existing 2-attempt retry (fresh manifest + fresh copies of both files) is exactly the right fix for that, so it stays as the narrower backstop the issue anticipated.
- One design note no longer applies: "the planner already fetches package.json uncached... the manifest could absorb that" — it doesn't anymore. `site/shared/version.js` now reads the version from the page's own DOM stamp (no fetch at all), so there's nothing to absorb.

## Also touched

- `scraper/README.md` and `site/plan/README.md`: the caching tables and prose described fixed TTLs; updated to describe the manifest instead (also fixed a stale "availability is allowed to fail" line in `site/plan/README.md` while in that paragraph — it hasn't been true since #309).
- `.claudinite/local/packs/edfringe-now/data-dir-is-generator-output.mjs` (+ its test): allowlisted `site/data/manifest.json` as a genuine `normalize.py` output, per that check's own fix instructions.

## Tests

- `site/shared/__tests__/data-cache.test.mjs`: rewritten for the manifest contract — hash-match serves from cache, a moved hash forces a re-fetch, each url tracks its own hash independently, a null/missing-key manifest never trusts the cache, plus the existing offline/corrupt-cache/quota fallback coverage carried over.
- `scraper/normalize.py --selftest`: new assertions that `write_json`'s returned hash matches the bytes on disk and is stable across an unchanged re-run, and that `build_manifest` sorts its output.
- `npm test` (327 tests) and `npm run test:ui` (134 UI goldens, real headless Chromium) both green locally — no golden moved, since the manifest fetch 404s gracefully against the frozen fixture set and every page degrades to its normal network-fetch path.
- `scripts/verify.sh` clean (0 blocking; the 2 advisories are pre-existing and unrelated — provenance backfill, wiki freshness).

No `Automerge:` field was set on #314 — opening this for review and stopping here, per the issue.

`--merge` now reconciles:

- A show id absent from a listing pass is marked `withdrawn: true` on the master (`reconcile_withdrawn`), never deleted — a show that returns needs no re-scrape.

**The completeness signal is the load-bearing part**, per the issue: reconciliation refuses to run unless `scraper/fetch_shows.py` itself attests the raw pass walked the *whole* listing. `fetch_shows.py` now writes `data/raw_pages/fetch_manifest.json` every run (`fetch_completeness`), and it's `complete: true` only when `recentlyAdded=ANY`, there's no `--max-pages` cap, no page failed, and every page is accounted for. `normalize.py`'s `load_fetch_manifest`/`reconcile_withdrawn` read it — absent, corrupt, or `complete: false` all refuse identically, and `--merge` still upserts normally, it just doesn't reconcile. Concretely: the daily top-up (`refresh-shows`, `--recently-added LAST_SEVEN_DAYS`) never reconciles, by design — it isn't a full walk. Reconciliation only ever engages on a `--recently-added ANY` pass run together with `--merge`, which today is a deliberate manual pairing (the currently-inert `scrape.yml` full-rebuild workflow runs `normalize.py` without `--merge` and replaces the master wholesale instead).

## Testing

- `python3 scraper/normalize.py --selftest` — extended to prove both directions: a complete pass reconciles (marks absent ids withdrawn, leaves present ones alone), and an absent/incomplete signal refuses (mutation-tested: temporarily reverted the `active_shows` filter and confirmed the new end-to-end assertion catches it).
- `site/plan/lib/__tests__/hydrate.test.mjs`'s master↔`shows.min.json` round-trip now compares against the master's *active* (non-withdrawn) shows, since a withdrawn show never reaches the wire at all; added a case guarding that a withdrawn id never appears in `shows.min.json` (no-ops today since the committed master has no withdrawn shows yet, guards the field once one exists).
- `npm test` (321 tests), `npm run test:ui` (134 tests, since the diff touches `site/`), and `npm run verify` all green.

## Deliberately left out

- Wiring an actual recurring "full pass + `--merge`" invocation into a task/workflow. The 2026 festival is over (per the owner's issue comment) — nothing withdrawn is being served today — so this is the mechanism for before next August, not a scheduled job. The full-rebuild workflow (`scrape.yml`) stays as-is (inert, no `--merge`); changing its invocation shape felt like a separate call for the owner to make.
- Per `--merge` reconciling and the issue explicitly having no `Automerge:` field ("this changes the generator behind the served data, and a reconciliation bug deletes the festival"), this PR is left open for review rather than delivered/merged — see #295 for the park this lands as.
